sources.entry: ptpython - Advanced Python REPL built on top of the python-prompt-toolkit.

summary.one_liner: prompt_toolkit is a pure-Python library for building interactive command-line applications, with ptpython (an advanced Python REPL) built on top of it.
summary.what_it_does: The library provides building blocks for interactive terminal programs, including a simple prompt() function for reading input. It supports syntax highlighting while typing (for example via a Pygments lexer), multi-line input editing, and code completion. Key bindings can be Emacs or Vi style, including some Vi features such as named registers and digraphs. It also offers incremental history search, auto-suggestions, text selection for copy/paste, bracketed paste, mouse support, and multiple input buffers. The README says it is designed to be a replacement for GNU readline, and that its only dependencies are Pygments and wcwidth.
use_cases: build a custom interactive command-line application
replace GNU readline in a Python shell
add syntax-highlighted input prompts to a CLI tool
create multi-line code editing in a terminal
notable: Pure Python with only Pygments and wcwidth as dependencies
Emacs and Vi key bindings, including Vi named registers and digraphs
Incremental reverse and forward history search, plus fish-style auto-suggestions
Works with Unicode double-width characters such as Chinese input
No global state, so multiple independent instances can coexist in one process
caveats: Windows support is best on recent Windows 10 builds; the Unix experience is described as somewhat better
README describes the Windows implementation as a 'best effort of what is possible'
